utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, IT-95-16-T, The Prosector versus Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, Dragan Papic and Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning. Counsel Puliselic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I forgot yesterday to tender exhibits into evidence from numbers D4/5 to D10/5, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I assume there is no objection. They are admitted into evidence. Thank you, Counsel Puliselic. And I will call upon Counsel Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Thank you, good morning Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, I have several questions for you linked to the accused Vlatko Kupreskic. Let me begin with the 16th of April, 1993. During your testimony yesterday you said that on the 16th of April, 1993, in the morning, you heard gunfire and headed with your family to the shelter?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Will you tell me what time it was when you left your house?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was about quarter to 6.00 or 6.00. I can't recall exactly, but about that time, quarter to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Tell me, please, how far is this shelter from your home?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is about 200 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Can you tell us, then, when you reached the shelter, what time it was?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was about five to 6.00 or 6.00, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Will you tell us now how much time you spent in the shelter, that is how long you stayed there until what time?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I stayed until -- I stayed about ten to twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Who did you find in the shelter when you reached it? Was it empty or were there people there already?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was almost full, but people were still arriving, people who started fleeing later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Were those people women, children, elderly people, and people not fit for military service?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, mostly. Mostly civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you know Vlatko Kupreskic and the members of his family?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you see any members of Vlatko Kupreskic's family in the shelter, and if you did, please tell us whom?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. When I got there to put my family in a safe place, I saw Vlatko Kupreskic, his wife and children, his mother. I saw two of his uncles. Among the many other people, they were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Once more, will you tell us what time it was when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was about 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: You said that you saw Vlatko Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Can you describe what he looked like or, rather, how he was dressed? Was he wearing civilian clothes, a uniform, was he armed?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was in civilian clothes and he was unarmed. He was not armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Were you surprised to find Vlatko Kupreskic in a shelter for people unfit for military service?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, I knew that Vlatko was unfit for military service. I know that he had some kind of heart surgery, and I know that he could not serve in the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you ever see him in uniform or carrying arms?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you, perhaps, know whether Vlatko acted politically ever or spoke in public?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you know what Vlatko engaged in at the time?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In commerce. He had a big wholesale store.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you get your supplies from him?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you know, at the time did Vlatko give his customers goods on credit?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did he make any distinction between Croat and Muslim customers or, rather, did he give Muslims goods on the same terms?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I should like for a moment the sound to be switched off so that we can go into private session, as I may be mentioning some names. Just for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. (Private session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: (Open session)

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: What is the name of your establishment, sir?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Cafe Victoria.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And I believe that is located close to another cafe about 40 metres away called the -- known popularly as Pican (pronounced phonetically) cafe, that is correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not Pican (pronounced phonetically), Pican.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Forty metres, yes. It is on the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And did that cafe also enjoy a similar clientele to yours?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't go there a lot but roughly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, you said that earlier in 1992 you volunteered to fight at the frontlines, and you and your son did so for four to five days; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. That was once early in 1992. We went as there were -- there wasn't much choice, and we reported as volunteers to go there for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did that volunteering, in fact, make you at that time a member of the HVO forces? Did they induct you into the HVO forces for doing that duty?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you receive any issue of weapons, or pieces of uniform or equipment when you reached the lines?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the front, yes. On the frontlines, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: When you left the frontlines to return home were you able to keep any of the equipment you were given or the clothing?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I didn't have equipment, I was just given a rifle, and when I went back I left that rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: You then formed the village guards in your own community with others. When did you first form the village guard?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. I know it was early in '92, so I'm unable to recall the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Was that an initiative by Mr. Nenad Santic who became its sort of overall commander, or was that just a getting together of local people?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. We had a meeting together, us and the Muslims, and we heard that some terrorists had entered a village near Turbe, so all of us together agreed to organise these village guards and to keep watch duty at night so that the same thing wouldn't happen in our surroundings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: How many people joined your village guard from the Croat side?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were about 30 to 40 of us. These were mostly elderly men. There were few young people there among them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I'll just ask you, were, in fact, Dragan Papic or Drago Josipovic members of the village guard?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Drago Josipovic, yes. Dragan Papic was further away from us. He wasn't near our village, so he wasn't a member of our village guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you structure those guards at that time as to two separate ethnic guards, one made up of Croat persons and the other made up of Muslim persons?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. We kept duty together. We were equal. We were like one in those days.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: How many people would form a guard on a given night in a particular patrol? How many would you go out with?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Every night. There would be ten men on duty and they would be there all night, and we took turns.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: By "all night," between which hours did you actually serve that duty? When did you start, when did you finish?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We would start in the evening at nightfall and we'd go home when it dawned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Would this be a mobile patrolling of the village, going round as a group, or did you station yourself in a particular place and just remain there for a period of time, like a checkpoint sort of thing?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We had a house where we stayed, all of us together, and then three men would patrol the area, then another three would go round and that is how we took turns.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And what roughly was the territorial area? Perhaps, in fact, I could resort to the exhibit already on the ELMO, with your leave. Could you look at that map on the machine next to you and could you indicate roughly the area that your guard covered with its patrols?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Would you like me to mark the circle?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I wouldn't say necessarily you have to mark it, it's not my exhibit to be marked, but just -- would you just point with your finger or the pointer if you have it there, please, but don't actually mark on the document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On this side of the road were half Muslims and half Croats, and then we covered this area, from here, then we would go along this path almost as far as Radak's bridge, then we would turn back and come round here as far as the shelter. So that would be the circle that we made. There's the sports centre, this group of houses. In other villages there were other guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Thank you. And as regards the -- that time, earlier in 1992, it was a mixed guard of Muslims and Croats who would carry out this duty?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And at that time when it was still a mixed unit, was Nenad Santic effectively your superior to whom you reported?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And how often did you communicate at that time with Mr. Nenad Santic?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Frequently, because his house was nearby and he would keep watch with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you know whether there was any liaison between Mr. Nenad Santic and anywhere else, any other areas, any other guards, any other military?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't have access to any such information, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Were you armed in these patrols?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Some people had permits for pistols or hunting rifles, those of us who were huntsmen but we didn't all have weapons. Then some people would carry a pole, another one a rifle and that is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: As for yourself, sir, did you have a sporting gun, or a pistol or a hunting rifle?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So did you, in fact, borrow any kind of weapon from somebody, or did you carry a pole or something like that?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had a neighbour, his name was Marko Santic, he was a hunter and he would regularly give me his gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, did you acquire any form of uniform in order to carry out these guard duties, like a camouflage jacket or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, you say that later on the Muslim residents formed a separate guard; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The separation started immediately after the first conflict in Ahmici, that is, after the elections. As soon as the nationalist structures were formed people started separating.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I believe you commented earlier that virtually everybody took a kind of ethnic standpoint at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: When you said that the separation came about, I recall you saying that everybody had to take a kind of ethnic stance after those elections. In other words, to lie with their own ethnic group; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't say that they had to, but I said that everyone started to align themselves with their own parties. There was the SDA, the HDZ, the SDS and in the smaller places and settlements people started separating along those lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: In fact, as you say, a local Muslim guard was formed, and was that, in fact, formed out of the local TO people who had been there before?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. The guards were formed on the basis of the SDA party.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I believe you said a Mr. Mehmed Ahmic was the commander of that village guard; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was commander of the village guard, but he was the most important person in Ahmici. He had the main say. He was the leading politician in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: You became aware, I presume, in mid 1992 of the creation and existence of the HVO, the Croatian Defence Council; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was not aware of it until the beginning of the conflict, that the HVO had been formed, though I would see people in uniform now and then. We were far away. We were not in Vitez. We were rather remote. So I didn't see any of those units.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Well, we've heard that during the latter part of 1992 and in early 1993, there was quite a build-up of people who would be wearing uniforms around the place. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And I believe, obviously, in your cafe and the nearby establishment, presumably a number of your customers started to be wearing various uniforms as well, is that not so?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: All those young men who were wearing uniforms, they went to the frontline. Rarely did they have time to visit cafes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Anyway, to get back to the village guard situation --

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: -- do you recall in mid to late 1992 Nenad Santic wore a uniform when he worked with you or you had dealings with him?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, let me see. Several young men had camouflage jackets or jeans. This was customary. They got hold of them somehow. But I can't remember precisely whether I saw Nenad Santic in a uniform. Someone would get a jacket, someone else trousers, but this was something that we could not get hold of.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, in October -- on the 20th of October, 1992, you said there was an outbreak of conflict when the roadblock put up by the Muslims was forcibly removed by the HVO. Do you recall that day, sir?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said that a conflict occurred when units from Kiseljak and Busovaca were heading for the defence of Jajce. I didn't say whether the roadblock was removed. That is something that I did not say. Maybe you misunderstood me. I didn't say whether they were removed or not. I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So will we agree that it was all to do with a checkpoint that was set up by the Muslims that apparently this conflict occurred; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, the conflict occurred because they wouldn't allow those units to pass towards Jajce.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Where were you on the morning of the 20th of October, 1992? Were you at your business?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I was in my shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you remain there for the whole of the morning?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, all morning, and I heard from local people that this conflict had occurred. People dropped in and they told me about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Were any of the people who dropped in people in uniform?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: When in the day did you first learn that this thing had taken place?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Immediately afterwards when the shooting started. We all wondered what it was. Then the Croats who were there in Ahmici, when the shooting started they fled, those that were unarmed, and that is how we learn that the conflict had occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, as a member of the village guard, did you think of taking any particular action to go out and check the situation for yourself?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, because I didn't have access to this. I didn't have the weapons, nor did anyone force me to do that, nor did I feel the need to do anything. I didn't really know what the factual state was, why it had occurred. It was only later on that I learnt that these units wanted to go to Jajce and that a conflict had broken out.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you have any means of communication with Mr. Nenad Santic at that time? Could you have telephoned, or did you have a portable phone or something?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had a telephone, but I didn't communicate by telephone. Very often the lines were down. They were probably digging, so that there was damage to the telephone lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Well, you said that you had constantly feared the incursion of terrorists, particularly by night, and that's why you formed the village guards?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did any thoughts of this being some form of terrorist incursion first occur to you when you heard the shooting and before you were told what was going on?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. When the conflict occurred, the first one in Ahmici, as we were close with the Muslims -- in fact we had tied our flags together -- I thought it was a Serb attack. I never thought that there was a conflict between the Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And yet you are saying that you did not take any steps to contact your fellow village guard members or Mr. Santic at that point?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, we didn't go anywhere. Nenad Santic was working at the gas station. He wasn't home during the day. He was working in Vitez, at the petrol station.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, after the 20th of October, did you hear anything about the surrender of weapons by Muslim residents in the area? Surrender of weapons to the HVO?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: During that period, from October through, let us say now, to January of 1993, were terrorist incursions the only concerns that you had that prompted carrying on with the village guards? Or were there other problems?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were other problems, because the guards became separate, and we never knew from which quarter danger could come.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: During that period, what was the situation as regards the local crime rate? Was there an increase in crimes against people or against property?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, there wasn't, at least in my immediate surroundings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I appreciate that you weren't in Vitez, but Vitez is not a very long way away. Did you hear anything about the events in Vitez at that time?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Was it true that --

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I heard that there might be a burglary into a store; things like that. There were plenty of such incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you ever hear about young men getting into uniform and forming sort of independent kind of units and going around town rampaging and committing crime in town, in Vitez? Did you ever hear anything about that?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I didn't. Because this was something that didn't reach us, especially the older people. We wouldn't hear such things.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: But this, you say, wasn't happening in your area?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you know the nearby village -- I hope I pronounce it correctly -- of Nadioci?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It's quite far from me, but I do know it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And were you aware of, I believe, a restaurant there at one time called the Bungalow?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you ever hear anything later, in, say, early 1993, about a military HVO unit or police unit being based at the Bungalow? Let's say around February '93.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, you see, as there was the Muslim checkpoint near the cemetery, people -- civilians couldn't pass by. And I personally had not heard about such a unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So if I were to just give you the name "the Jokers," I believe in the language is "Jokeri," would that name ring any kind of bell with you?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: For me, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, you're saying, sir, that therefore in early 1993, civilian movement was severely restricted because of this checkpoint; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Not just at one spot; there were these checkpoints everywhere, so that it was very difficult to move around, especially for civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Is it true to say that some of those checkpoints were manned by Muslim people in military dress and some by Croat people in military dress? There were different checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Let me tell you, my route was Karlo Vrebac, who had a wholesale store, and Vlatko Kupreskic also, and those were the places I visited, plus guard duty in Zume. So I didn't move further than that. I heard that there were checkpoints everywhere. In the Muslim villages they were controlled by Muslims, and so on. There were these checkpoints everywhere, so I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: By that time, you presumably were familiar with the expression of the HVO, or the Croatian Defence Council, by February or March of 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, were you aware of the existence of any BiH army units in the village of Ahmici, let us say in March of 1993? Any units stationed there or quartered there?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. As there was a large number of displaced persons from Jajce, from Karaula, and so on, it became -- life became very difficult. There were provocations. When these persons arrived, they constituted a large majority. So there were all kinds of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: But with respect the question I asked you was were you aware of any formal Bosnian army BiH units that were stationed in and around Ahmici -- not refugees -- of Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, yes. All those refugees immediately joined in the defence and the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, let us move on, if I may, to the 15th of April, the day before, I understand, the big conflict in Ahmici. Can you tell me what time you started work that morning?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I usually opened at 9 or 10 a.m. Never early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And how long that day did you stay open to do business?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Until midnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: You say you closed at midnight; did you at any time perform any village guard duty during that evening?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And between which hours did you do that?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't -- I wasn't -- there were others, because it wasn't my turn to keep guard duty. It was -- the guard was held that evening as usual.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I see. Yes, the question I should have expressed more clearly to you, sir, was did you yourself go out on village guard duty at all that night?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, you therefore had, did you, a normal day and evening of trading?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I did my everyday tasks, my usual business.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you have many customers in your establishment during the course of that evening?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, so-so. I never had very many. The customers would come and go. It's a rural area; there were never many customers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Can you recall the mood of your customers that evening? Was it any different to other evenings? Was there any particular anxiety or concern amongst your customers?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, they talked only about Zivko Totic, who had been taken prisoner, and the killing of his companions. That's what was discussed. Everything else was as usual.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So at what time did you finally go to sleep that night?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I worked until midnight, and as soon as I came home, I went to bed at once.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Would it be true to say that when you went to bed that night, you appear not to have been concerned that there was any kind of potential violence about to break out in your vicinity?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: It's true to say, is it, that there was no prior indication to you as a resident of Zume, or the people in your area, that there was an impending attack by the army of BiH, or anyone else? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No one knew about it. None of us knew about something like that or expected something like that to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Had you seen any activity of armed forces people, HVO or ABiH, during the day of the 15th of April? Did you see any troop movements or vehicles or artillery, or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I was a little way away from the main road, and you usually hear vehicles passing by. But that was usual; I didn't pay attention to the kind of vehicles passing along the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, you say you awoke at about 05.30 in the morning to the sound of gunfire; is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: You then -- we have heard the timing, and what you then did with your family, going to the shelter and so forth. But it seems it was probably therefore about 10 past 6 outside the shelter that you met Mr. Nenad Santic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And what was Mr. Nenad Santic wearing when you encountered him near the shelter?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was wearing some kind of camouflage jacket and civilian trousers. And he met me and he talked in a hurried way. He said, "Leave your wife and children immediately and go to guard the bridge, Radak's bridge."

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did he give you any reason for guarding that bridge? Did he say why he specifically wanted that bridge guarded?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, he told me, "Ivo, there has been a conflict between the Muslims and the Croats, and the main road, the Busovaca/Vitez road, has been blocked off at Ljuba's houses. There's no way through, so we have to guard this bridge. Nothing must happen there under any conditions. Go and guard that bridge. You will find Drago Vidovic and Dragan Papic there."

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: He didn't go into any other kind of details as to what specific forces or persons were involved in this action?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, he didn't say anything. This is all he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: In order to guard the bridge, did you do anything about trying to obtain a weapon or something?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, Nenad Santic brought us two M-48 rifles. That's what we had at the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: You say he brought them; in other words, did he come later and bring them to you at the bridge?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, when we arrived there, he came some 15 minutes later and brought us these two M-48 rifles, and he issued orders that no one was to move away from the bridge. So that we were not allowed to leave the bridge. We could move between Radak's bridge and the house where we rested, some 50 metres up and down.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, could you state to me again, sir, please, from that point when you were assigned to the bridge, who exactly was with you at that point when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I arrived at Radak's bridge, I found Drago Vidovic there. And Dragan Papic wasn't there immediately, only about 10 minutes later, Dragan Papic arrived from the direction of Donja Rovna. We were surprised to see him coming from that direction and asked him why, and he said he had been taking his mother, his wife, and his sister to the shelter there. And then he joined us there, and we remained there at the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So there were now in fact three of you at the bridge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did Mr. Papic bring a weapon with him?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did Mr. Papic say he'd been instructed to come and guard the bridge?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: You were aware, sir, that Mr. Papic, as a forester, did possess a weapon, a hunting rifle with a scope?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't know that. I know that as a forester, he had a rifle; but whether it was his or whether it belonged to the forestry company, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: But you say you've never seen him carrying it in town?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, people didn't carry rifles around the town then. He usually went toward the forests.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: But isn't it true that in the months just before April, 1993 there were more people around in uniform and there were people seen carrying guns in and around your area; is that not so?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I was there and I didn't really have much opportunity to see these people. There may have been such people or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So the three of you were at that bridge on the 16th of April, and you just had the two rifles between you, correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: How many of you stayed on duty at one point and how many took rest during that day; was it two on and one off or one on and two off?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was usually two who kept guard and one who rested.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: How long would the rest period be?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, it was not limited. If anyone felt tired, they would go and take a rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So essentially the guard duty on the bridge was conducted as a two man exercise, two on duty, one guy would take a rest?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there was a house there where we could rest and when someone got tired we would wake up the one who was resting and then the -- they would change.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Was any provision made in the course of that day, the 15th -- I'm so sorry, the 16th, was there anything done in the course of that day to arrange for some relief for you people; in other words, some replacements or others to join you?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Were you given supplies of food and ammunition?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We had stocks of food because the woman in the house cooked for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And ammunition, were you supplied with some?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We had a few packets of ammunition for the M48 rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, we have seen the location of that house, and when one of you went off to rest there, would the other two then just walk up and down on the river bank as you indicated on the photographs?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. We would go 50 metres in one direction, 50 in the other, and around the house and the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: What was the name, if I may ask, of the lady at the house who cooked for you?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The woman was the wife of a man called Ljubas. I don't know her name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that you'd had, obviously, orders to stay at the bridge and guard it, but --

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: -- were you told how long you would have to remain there on that first day? Did they say how long they thought you would have to stay and guard?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Nothing was told us, only that we had to keep the bridge secure and that we were not to leave it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: At that time, to the best of your knowledge, sir, I suppose your family was still in the shelter and your business was obviously unattended because the conflict had broken out. Yes?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. The building was locked up and no one was there either in my house or my business premises.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you have any concerns that you would have liked to have gone back to your house just to check later in the day that it was all right?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. No. Nenad Santic would visit us quite often and he told me that my family was in the shelter and that there was nothing for me to worry about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I believe you said yesterday that in your case you stayed there until August guarding the bridge?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I stayed there at the bridge until the 24th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: All right. But during that period were you given any opportunities to go back to your business, to see your family, to check on your home?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I never left the bridge. A few times at night my wife would come to see me and tell me that everything was all right, but I did not have approval to go home and I could not go home. And that's why I fell ill. I suddenly fell ill. I vomited blood and I had to go for treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, sir, if I can go back to that first day. You worked through the 16th of April and you say you arrived somewhere around 7 -- between 6.30 and 7.00, you feel, at the Radak bridge; is that so?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I worked on the 15th, not on the 16th.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I probably misled you in the way I put the question. I'll do it again, sir. On the day, the 16th, you arrived at the bridge at about 6.30 to 7.00, that I believe is what you said.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I said that I arrived at Radak's bridge at about 20 past 6.00 or half past 6.00, somewhere around that time. I couldn't be very precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Presumably, between the three of you, you kept guard duty going right through the night, 24 hours night and day? Yes?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Because I already said that one always rested while two kept watch.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Were you on the second day, say the 17th or were you on the 18th joined by any others to swell your numbers beyond the three?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there were some others keeping watch on the other side of the bridge. Those were from the Busovaca municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: But with regard to your own side of the bridge, did any additions or replacements come in, say, the two or three days following the 16th?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did Mr. Dragan Papic express any concerns to you regarding his domestic situation at home; his wife was heavily pregnant, there had been fighting going on in Ahmici? Was he worried?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, he was worried. He told me that his wife was heavily pregnant, but that he had taken her to a safe place, to the shelter in Rovna, and there were no problems there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: When Mr. Nenad Santic paid visits to you, did he speak to Dragan Papic? Did he relay family messages or, you know, report to him as he did to you?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. His family was in the Busovaca municipality and Nenad Santic didn't go to the Busovaca municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you recall whether Mr. Dragan Papic left the location at any time during, say, the three days through the 16th, 17th or 18th of April?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that he didn't. No one was allowed to leave that guard post.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Even though one may have orders, it is sometimes possible people disobey them. I am just asking whether at any time Mr. Papic may have left?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It's not possible, and we are certain that no one left the guard post.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: You said you were taking a rest period in the lady's house, and the other two were guarding the bridge, and if those two started to walk down the river bank, would it be possible to leave that house and go back down the road towards Zume without being seen by your colleagues? I am just saying would that have been possible at that site?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it wasn't possible, because we moved only within a circumference of 50 metres, and the house is less than 20 metres away from the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: But, clearly, there were periods of time when any one of you was out of the sight of the other, if only to be inside that house?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We were always able to see him. He couldn't have left the house, except through the garage door, and it was always within our sight. And if he had left, how could he have -- he wouldn't have been able to come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Can you recall the day when Mr. Papic was ordered, you know, to leave that duty?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He wasn't ordered, but I remember he stayed with us eight to ten days and then he told us that his wife was either having a baby or had had the baby, I'm not sure exactly which, and then he went home and they never saw him again until after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Well, let me get this clear. Had you received any message or had there been a visit by Nenad Santic or anybody to say that Mr. Papic could go home?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, yes, Nenad Santic came, and he told him he could go home, and then he left. And the two of us stayed there alone, on our own.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: From that time forward you say it reduced to the two of you, yourself and Mr. Drago Vidovic -- Dragan Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did he remain, indeed, until August along with you?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, he stayed after I left, when I went for treatment, and I don't know whether he was joined by anyone else after I left. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: You said that Mr. Dragan Papic was a regular visitor to your establishment; is that so?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So, to that extent, as a customer you knew him quite well?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, since he worked as a forester, he would go to his job and he would always drop in.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: We have heard that some witnesses have indicated that in the course of his work Mr. Papic was often seen in a camouflage kind of kit or a very dark uniform type of kit, even black, as quite regular clothing in the months before the conflict. Do you recall him being dressed in that way?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, until the conflict broke out, Dragan Papic was employed in the forestry and he always wore a camouflage jacket and a green uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: How green was that? Was it a light green or very dark or mid-green?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, maybe like this colour here (indicating). It's a forestry uniform, it's green. Every forester wore a green uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: A bit like the microphone button, that kind of green? You pointed to that.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. It was that kind of colour. For example, like these headphones here, or like this canvas. I can't explain it clearly, but it was always a green uniform for foresters.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: You say that on the frequent visits he was going to and from the forest you don't recall Mr. Papic carrying his weapon with him?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, he always carried a rifle when he was on his way to the forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: You said you weren't aware of the gender of his wife's baby after these events. Did you not have any contact with Mr. Papic as a customer after the conflict?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, no. No. To tell you the truth, I don't know today even about his children. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: If I may, I would like to take you back a moment to the 16th of April itself. You stated that you arrived at the shelter, which was full of Croatian ethnic persons, both men and women. That's correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there were both men and women, elderly people, children, minors, and so on, and those refugees were still coming in to the shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I believe you stated Mr. Marko Santic was in the shelter at that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, all the elderly people. This was the man I borrowed the rifle from, when I went on guard duty. They were all there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: You have said that at that time of day, approximately 06.00, you saw Mr. Vlatko Kupreskic in the shelter. That is clear?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: You say you remained about ten minutes or so, between 06.10 and 06.15, and you had left the shelter. Was Mr. Vlatko Kupreskic still there?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, all of them stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: For the remainder of that day did you -- did you see Mr. Vlatko Kupreskic at any time?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't see him again. On that day I didn't see him again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Because, of course, you left for the Radak bridge and did you not revisit the shelter or go away from that bridge for the whole of the rest of that day?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't have the chance to see Vlatko again because I was at the bridge and I was not allowed to move away from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So the only thing you can state with certainty here is you know where Vlatko Kupreskic was just before ten past 6.00 that morning?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Thank you. When you were in the shelter, did you exchange words with any of the people there? Did you speak to any of them?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I spoke to the refugees who were just arriving. Those who were closer to the border of Ahmici. The Croats living closer to Ahmici, they were all fleeing in our direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you, in fact, exchange any words with Mr. Vlatko Kupreskic?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, because Vlatko was already in the shelter when I arrived, so I didn't talk to him at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I believe you stated in your evidence that the Croatian women told you that there had been heavy fighting because of Muslim units that had attacked Ahmici. That was the story you were given; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is true that I said that Muslim units from Ahmici had attacked the Croatian houses, and that they said that Mirjan Santic had been killed in the conflict in the morning. That's all I learned from those women, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So what you're saying now is you were told that Mirjan Santic had been killed in the conflict. The women didn't say anything about heavy casualties on both sides?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, they didn't mention that. That morning I didn't know anything about heavy casualties, I just heard about Mirjan Santic. But later I learned that there were many casualties on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Have you ever endeavoured to verify what you were told as being true and accurate?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I didn't move from the Radak bridge, nor did I have any chance of verifying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: If I were to say to you, sir, that the evidence indicated a large quantity of Muslim civilian casualties, would that come as a surprise to you or be something you may have heard subsequently?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It wouldn't be a surprise because I heard that there were many casualties on both sides, so I wouldn't be surprised at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Then it would be a surprise to you, sir, if, in fact, in Ahmici, on the 16th of April, there were hardly any Croat casualties recorded, maybe only two or three people? How would you react to that proposition, sir?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. As far as I was informed, there were casualties on both sides. I really had no access to the facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: There's one thing I would like to ask you now, sir, about the shelter itself. Can you give a physical description of what that shelter comprised? How deep in the ground it was, whether it had any -- what access indoors and windows and things, can you tell me, please?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I can, I can. It was a house with two storeys, and the cellar was dug into the ground and you went down some steps to reach it. As for windows, in such a short time I really didn't pay any attention to see whether there were any openings, I just remember that the entrance was large. You went down some steps and then you entered through a big door.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Can you give any indication of the dimensions, how wide and how long the room was?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was about ten metres -- about ten -- no, about a hundred square metres. Ten by ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Ten by ten. And can you indicate what the state of the light was in there, or what lighting it had?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It had electric lighting, and I can't remember whether it was on or whether it was daylight already. I think it probably was still on. The electrical lights were on, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Just a moment to confer if I may, Your Honours. I'm trying to be as expeditious as possible. I just literally have about three more questions, Your Honours, which will be convenient for your break time, Mr. President. Mr. Vidovic, I have just a couple more questions for you. Could you just confirm again for me who the other guards were at the other end of the Radak bridge? I do believe you've given their names but I'd just like them confirmed if you'd be so kind.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There was Zvonimir Santic and Jozo Alilovic, but there were more of them only but I don't know them. But among all of them I knew Zvonimir Santic and Jozo Alilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you recall if they were in full uniforms?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Sorry, by that you mean no, they were not or no, you do not remember?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They had civilian dress. We could see each other well because the bridge is not a big one, so we could see each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: But you say you don't recall the names of the other people who came. Did they come and go as well? Did they have others with them?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They also changed, they took turns, but Zvonimir Santic and Jozo Alilovic were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you recall how long they stayed at the bridge? Was it a matter of just days or weeks?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: For the first 20 days or so all of them stayed there, and afterwards things changed. I don't know. They changed more than we did. We didn't change, as we didn't have replacements.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Were there, in fact, any incidents at the bridge during your guarding time there, particularly any kind of shootings or injuries occurring?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, let me see. From the Muslim lines there was a three-barrelled gun, so it was not possible to cross the bridge, and as soon as a vehicle came or something, the bridge would be shelled. Their aim was probably to destroy the bridge because they knew that this was our corridor. Those were the incidents that occurred, no others.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Just a couple more things if you would be so kind. I have four names I would like to mention to you, as to whether these are people whom you know. The first is Zdranko Pranjkovic. Is that name familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Stipica Santic?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There are several Stipica Santic, so I couldn't answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Zeljko Grbavac?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Finally, Ivica Krizanac?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Finally, sir, were you acquainted with a lady called Senada Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: You didn't have a neighbour by that name, or a similar name that I may be mispronouncing?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Maybe I did, but I don't know. No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. That concludes the cross-examination by the Prosecution. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. We will take a 30-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Puliselic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: I will ask you a few additional questions. In your testimony you said that it was not permitted to leave your positions at Radak bridge.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You said that Dragan Papic did not move away from that position for some ten days, that is, until the time his wife delivered a baby.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: My question refers to two specific dates, the 16th and the 17th of April, 1993. Are you quite certain, 100 per cent sure, that on the 16th and the 17th of April Dragan Papic did not leave his position as a guard?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm 100 per cent sure that Dragan Papic did not leave that position for the first eight days of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In view of the position you held at Radak's bridge, and you said that Ahmici could not be seen from there, could you tell us on what day was the gunfire from Ahmici loudest?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was loudest on the 16th, the day the conflict started.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Was there any gunfire on the 17th?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Can it be said that as time passed the shooting subsided?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. On the contrary. There was gunfire all the time. Not always in Ahmici but in other localities, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You said that Nenad Santic informed Dragan Papic that his wife had given birth, that he allowed him to leave that guard post. Did I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, you did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You also spoke about the other side of the bridge, the side near Donja Rovna, that the guards were rather more numerous there?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us how many guards you would see there, at least during the first few days?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were three or four of them, but two were there all the time, that is Zvonimir Santic and Jozo Alilovic, and I knew them personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So these were the people who spent the most time there?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. They were there all the time. Others took turns, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about Zvonko Santic being wounded during patrol duty, seriously wounded?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you learn subsequently that a comparative large number of Muslims were killed in Ahmici and that many houses were set on fire?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Mr. Vidovic, my learned friend the Prosecutor, in the course of his cross-examination, asked you to describe the shelter that you reached. I will now show you several photographs so as to hear your comments about them. Could I ask the usher to show the witness this photograph, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D20/3.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Could you tell me what is this a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is a photograph of a house and the entrance to the house and the shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Is this the elaborate entrance that you described?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown a second photograph, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D21/3.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Would you turn it round a little, please so that we can see it properly? That's right. That's right. That's fine. Could you tell me now what does this photograph show?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's right. It shows the way down to the shelter, down the steps.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Is that the entrance you described, from the corridor you go down some steps to reach it?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: But this was a long time ago. I never went to that house again, but roughly, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D22/3.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Can you tell us what is shown on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is the shelter where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you see the electric light that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you see the windows and the fact that the premise has been dug in?

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that is what can be seen on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I have no further questions, and I should like to tender these three photographs into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: You have to provide the Court and the Prosecution with copies, and only then can we admit them into evidence. So if you kindly give us tomorrow, provide us tomorrow copies, we will come back to this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Vidovic, thank you for giving evidence in Court. You may now be released. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IVO VIDOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Thank you. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Puliselic, any protective measures for the next witness, Goran Papic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Very well. If he could be brought in. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Papic. Could you please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Counsel Puliselic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Papic, good morning.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Will you please introduce yourself to Their Honours, your name, date and place of birth, and where you live?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: My name is Goran Papic. I was born on the 4th of December, 1975, in Travnik. I live in Vitez, in a place called Topola.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Is it a place called Topola, or is it a part of Santici?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is a part of Santici.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us how you are related to Dragan Papic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Dragan Papic is my older brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: How old were you in 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: In 1992 I was sixteen and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So you were a minor?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us who lived in your house at the time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: In our house in 1992 there was my father, Ivo; mother, Dragica; brother, Dragan; his wife, Ruzica; my older sister, Ivanka; and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: To your right is an aerial photograph of Ahmici and the surroundings. With the help of the pointer, could you please show us the house you lived in.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: This is the house we lived in. (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Who is the owner of that house?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: The owner of that house is my father, Ivo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the year your brother got married?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: My brother Dragan got married in August 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Could I ask the usher for his assistance, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D11/5.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Papic, what kind of document is this?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: It's a document that is a marriage certificate proving that on the 10th of August, 1991 --

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: -- Dragan Papic and Ruzica Lasta were married.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us where the marriage took place?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: In the church in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Were there many guests at the wedding?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were many guests at the wedding.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did the guests enjoy themselves? Were there any problems?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: There were no problems. It was a nice party, and it went on until late that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Where was the party held?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: In the backyard of our house. So the wedding was in Busovaca, and after the wedding the party took place in the garden of our house in Santici.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Were only Croats in attendance at the wedding, or were there Muslims as well?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No, there were Muslims too. We were all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you take photographs of that event?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, there's a videotape of the whole wedding ceremony.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: And the party?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, the wedding itself and the party that followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Who made this film?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: It was filmed by Mehmed Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did he use his own camera?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, the camera was owned by Mehmed Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Who was Mehmed Ahmic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: He was our next-door neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did he have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: His nickname was Sudjuka.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: How far is your house from his? Roughly.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Close to 60 metres. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Could you show us on the aerial photograph Mehmed Ahmic's house.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Mehmed Ahmic's house?

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: First show us your house and then his.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: This is our house, and this is Mehmed Ahmic's house (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Considering the fact that Mehmed Ahmic was invited to the wedding, and that he filmed the event with his video camera, I assume that your brother, Dragan Papic, was on very good terms with him.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, the entire family was on good terms with him, and we visited one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So he used to come to your house and you would visit his?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, we went to his house. We visited each other at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you do any favours for each other?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, when Mehmed Ahmic was building his new house, we helped him, we supplied him with the utilities he needed -- electricity, water -- free of charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So can you remember approximately when he was building this house? If you can remember. If not --

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: At the wedding we referred to, were there any other members of Mehmed Ahmic's family?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: He was there with his entire family at the wedding.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You said that there were other Muslims there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. All our neighbours, the entire Causevic family.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to your father's friend?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was a friend of my father's, and he still is. He is still my father's friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us approximately how many guests there were?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: At the wedding, was Fahrudin Ahmic there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Fahrudin Ahmic was there with his family.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did he live nearby? Can you show us his house on the aerial photograph?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Fahrudin Ahmic's house is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So, close to the wood?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, close to the wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Were your father and Dragan therefore on good terms with the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were on good terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: What was your father's occupation then?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: My father was a plumber at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Is he still a plumber?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, he is still a plumber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did he do plumbing for anyone who asked him to?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, for the entire village of Ahmici and the surroundings, he did all the plumbing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So he did the plumbing in Muslim houses as well?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, in Muslim houses too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know that it was he who set up the plumbing in the mosque?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, in both mosques it was he who did the plumbing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So in the one with the minaret and the one without it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did your brother Dragan sometimes help him when he had time? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, he helped him if he wasn't occupied with his own job. If he wasn't working, and if my father had a lot of work, he would help him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what Dragan Papic was by occupation?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: He was a forester.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: What kind of school did he finish?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: He finished school for forestry technicians.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: In Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know where he was employed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: He was employed in the Vitez forestry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, until when was he employed in the Vitez forestry, on a regular basis?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Until the beginning of the conflict, the 15th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know, or did he tell you, perhaps, what his job consisted of?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: His job consisted in preserving the wood and the game.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So he made sure that no one cut wood without permission?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how he was dressed when he went to his job? Did he always wear the same kind of clothes, or different clothes?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Well, he had his uniform, which was green, a forester's uniform, which he was issued when he got his job.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Apart from this uniform, did he ever wear any kind of camouflage jacket or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Well, with the beginning of the war with the Serbs, someone -- and I don't remember who -- gave him a camouflage jacket which he would wear sometimes with jeans. I don't remember him wearing any other kind of uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: When he went to the woods, did he sometimes carry a weapon?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, sometimes he carried a rifle with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: What kind of rifle was it? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Well, it was an ordinary rifle, M-48, which he had to carry because of wild animals.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you remember -- do you know whether it was his -- whether he owned it, or whether it belonged to the company?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: It was owned by the company.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know when Dragan did his service in the Yugoslavia People's Army? What year was it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: I think it was 1987 to 1988. I'm not sure, but I think that's when it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did he perhaps tell you about his return -- when he returned, sorry, from the JNA, or later, did he tell you what kind of weapons he had been trained to use?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember he talked about it. He said that he had learned to use infantry weapons and a 60-millimetre mortar which belongs to infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether Dragan at that time, while he was employed, whether he was a member of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No. He was not a member of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Why couldn't he be a member?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Because he was employed and no one asked him to join.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know where he was in the first day of the armed conflict, the conflict which started on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know. He kept guard at Radak's bridge and in the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did he get an official invitation?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't. He was sent there by Nenad Santic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: How did he send him? Who was Nenad Santic to send him there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
