utterances.text: Nenad Santic at that time was the commander of some kind of village guard or something like that. I don't know what his post was exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: How far is Radak's bridge, approximately, as the crow flies from your house?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: But do you know where Radak's bridge is?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Can you show it on the aerial photograph?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: This is Radak's bridge here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Can we see the river Lasva on the aerial photograph?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. It was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: To go back again to your brother's job. You said that he worked in the forestry until the 15th of April, 1993, that is until the beginning of the war?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether after the war he got a job somewhere?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know he got a job in Imprenacija in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know what this company dealt in?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Imprenacija is a company processing wood and producing products made of wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether your brother, Dragan Papic, is still in Imprenacija as their employee?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I believe he still is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Why was this decision made at the company? Do you know or can you assume?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Well, I think that the employees decided to help his family because his family has no other income, so in order to help his family they decided to keep him as an employee.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Dragan's wife is not employed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No, she is unemployed. She is a housewife.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask the usher to take the following documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D12/5.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Papic.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: This is a photocopy of a document. Can you tell us what it is?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: This is a photocopy of the employment book of Dragan Papic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Can you turn to the page showing his employment, page number 10, number 164 in the first column. What does it say? Until when was your brother employed in the ^ Lasvasunska forester's office?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: The 15th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: The next two boxes are empty. It says "deleted." Do you know what this refers to?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No. Possibly there was some kind of error.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Can it be seen at the end that he is now employed in Imprenacija?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. His employment started and then it continues on the next page: He was already at The Hague on these dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Apart from his job at the company or at the forestry office, was there anything else your brother did in his spare time? What was his hobby?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: His hobby, apart from his job, was repairing vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: He learnt to do this on his own?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was talented in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did he repair everybody's vehicles, regardless of whether they were Muslims or Croats or someone else?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, he repaired vehicles for all those who felt that he could, who trusted him. He would repair their vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether he was interested in political issues?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No, he was never interested in politics.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Well, he never expressed any political opinions or conclusions. I don't remember that he ever went to any political meetings. Sometimes he would watch on television, but he was never active in any other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So we can say that he was not active politically anywhere in the village?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No, no, he wasn't politically active anywhere. He didn't have any political posts --

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: He didn't have any political posts in Santici?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No, either in Santici or elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: In your home, do you know whether any kind of -- any kind of political meetings or military meetings were held?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No, there were no meetings. It was a family home. There were no meetings ever held there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did your brother, Dragan, have a lot of friends among the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, he had quite a few friends with whom he had grown up in Santici.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you know a person called Paco Nusret?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew Nusret Paco.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who he was?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Nusret Paco was a refugee who had been driven out from his village by the Serbs and he came to live in a house close to our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Was he a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did Dragan, your brother, associate with him?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, they spent time together. Nusret Paco would sometimes help him with the cars, although he didn't really know how to do this very well, but they were good friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Nusret Paco had a young child?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, he had a young child.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did Dragan do something for that child?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. He took milk for the child free of charge. When he had time he would go to fetch the milk, and when he wasn't there, my mother or my sister would take milk to them or he would come to fetch the milk himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Nusret Paco was unable to buy milk?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No, he was a refugee. He was in somebody else's house. He didn't have anything of his own.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Whose house was it? Was it an abandoned house or what?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: It was a weekend house belonging to Hamo who lived in Zenica, and Hamo would come there occasionally. Later he didn't need it, so, like many other people, he allowed refugees to use his house.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether your brother, Dragan, sometimes went to the mosque?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Well, if someone died or if there was a Muslim holiday, he would go there with his friends to the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did your father also --

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, but only when someone died.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you remember an event in October, 1992, I am referring to the first conflict between the Muslims and the Croats?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember the first conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how it came about and what really happened that day?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: On that day, the 20th of October, 1992, Muslim units, organised and armed, set up a roadblock at the cemetery and dug trenches to stop the HVO from Busovaca and Kiseljak who were on their way to help Jajce, which was about to fall. There was a conflict because they stopped the HVO, so there was a conflict between the HVO and the armed Muslim units in which there were Muslims from Ahmici who were leading the other Muslims from the other villages who had come to help them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So the HVO from Busovaca and Kiseljak were going to help the HVO in Jajce?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know who, or what do you think caused the conflict, whose fault was it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: The Muslims caused the conflict on that day and that conflict is their fault.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did any of the Croats from the area of Ahmici, do you know, take part in this armed conflict?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No. The Croats, the villagers didn't know what it was about or what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Were any houses damaged in that conflict?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, two houses were damaged and, perhaps, some farm buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So together with the farm buildings, altogether it would be five, six buildings?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, five or six buildings in total were damaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether on that occasion anyone was wounded or killed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know that of the Muslims, Pezer Halid was killed. Of the Croats, a young man whose surname was Vidovic, who was from Kiseljak, I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You mentioned Pezer Halid. Do you know where he was killed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was killed -- he was killed near the cemetery in the trench that had been dug by the Muslims that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you know Halid Pezer well? Were you on good terms with him?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I had known him all my life and we had been friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you go to the same school?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, we went to the same school, but he was older than me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: How much older?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Maybe a year or year and a half. I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Was Halid Pezer a soldier of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No, he was messenger for Mehmed Ahmic and Zaid Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mehmed Ahmic also known as Sudjuka?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was Sudjuka's messenger and Zaid Ahmic's messenger.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Who was Zaid Ahmic, who was this person? Did he belong to the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was a member of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, who was among the first soldiers from Ahmici to join the army of BiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You said that you knew Halid Pezer well. Can you tell us whether his parents had any kind of problems with him?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, they had problems because the Muslims from Ahmici went to the war front in Visoko and Mehmed Ahmic and Zaid Ahmic organised this. I remember Halid wanted to go and his parents didn't allow him to go, and he had a row with his parents and ran away from home. He didn't come back for two days. Then he came back and I don't know what happened after that. But I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: At the time of this conflict on the 20th of October, 1992, was your father, Ivo Papic, at home?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No, my father was in Split on that day. He was visiting a house we have in Split.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: In Split?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: In Split. In a suburb of Split in Kastel Gomilica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So your father was not at home on the 20th of October. What about the others?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: All of us were at home. My brother, Dragan, his wife, my sister and I, we were at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: And then you heard gunfire. Did you hear gunfire?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, the gunfire woke us up and then we all got up. At that moment we were most frightened by the words we could hear coming from the loud speaker on the mosque, "Croats, give yourself up and give up your weapons." Then we started fleeing the house. I was the last to stay in the house. I fled and a shot came from the direction of Mehmed Ahmic's house toward me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: These words, "Croats, give yourself up," was that during a lull in the gunfire?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, the gunfire was a little way away and the mosque was close to our house, so we could hear it clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Is there a loud speaker on the mosque?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, there is a loud speaker which they use for their prayers, their daily prayers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You said that a shot came at you from Mehmed Ahmic's house?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, from the direction of Mehmed Ahmic's house, a shot was fired at me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Where were the other members of the family? Where did they go?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: They fled to the woods. I was frightened. I returned to the house. I stayed there for a brief time. Then I ran out again into a hedge, and then I followed my family behind the hedge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you find them in the woods?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No. They had already left. I found my relatives, Zoran and Ivica, and my brother had told them to wait for me, and my brother took my mother, wife and sister and Zoran's mother, who was already in the woods, towards Rovna.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Why towards Rovna?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Because there were no Muslims in Rovna. There was no conflict. It was peaceful there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You said that you hid in the woods with your cousins and friends. Did you, perhaps, hear or see any kind of anti-aircraft gun in that woods which was used to fire at Mehmed Ahmic's house?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: There were no -- there was no such weapon near our house, because these were all family homes inhabited by women, children, the elderly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: But you were in the woods. Was there anything like that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No, there was nothing like it in the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Will you please show us on the aerial photograph the woods that you hid in?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: This is the wood that I hid in.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: When did you return home?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: I returned home during the night. When night fell we went back. We felt a little safer, though it was stupid of us to go back but we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you remember about what time did the shooting stop on the 20th of October?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: I cannot recollect exactly. Maybe about 4.00, 5.00 or 6.00. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You spoke about this wood, so I'd like to know whether that wood is owned by several people?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. This part of the woods is owned by five different persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Who owns the largest part of that wood?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: This part of the woods is owned by Simo Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Who are the other owners?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: There was Gavro Vidovic, then Anto Papic, Marija Papic and a small part owned by my father Ivo Papic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So the smallest part of the woods was owned by your father Ivo Papic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us roughly how far that wood is from Mehmed Ahmic's house is, roughly?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you exactly. I think up to a hundred metres. Maybe a little more. I can't tell you exactly, I never measured it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: I should like to ask the witness to be shown Prosecution Exhibit 61. Do you recognise the house on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: This is Mehmed Ahmic Sudzuka's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Is that how the house looked after the conflict of the 20th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No, it didn't. This house wasn't seriously damaged, only the right-hand side of the roof was damaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Could you show us with this pointer?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: This part was damaged, the back part of the roof on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, is that the eastern facade of the house?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: When did this damage occur, the damage shown on this picture?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: This damage was the result of the second conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: On the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Was Mehmed Ahmic in the house on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No, he was not in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So he had left earlier on?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. Because he was a member of the SDA party, immediately after the first conflict he got an apartment in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you learn subsequently, perhaps, from which direction Mehmed Ahmic's house was hit, that is, the eastern part of the roof?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. I learned several days after the event that I had been hit from the direction of Hrasno.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Was there talk that the shooting had come from Hrasno during that conflict?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. After the conflict we learned that a missile had been fired from Hrasno.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: The damage to the roof on the eastern side of the house, could it have been caused by any fire? Let us assume that there may have been an anti-aircraft gun in the wood. Could the damage have been caused on the roof by fire coming from that direction?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No, because from the wood you can only see the front part of the house and the house was hit at the back.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me anything about Mehmed Ahmic as a person? Did he change in any way?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Mehmed Ahmic was not very popular among his own Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Because he was a gambler. He would borrow money without paying it back, he did trade in stolen vehicles, so that he cheated quite a large number of people, both Muslims and Croats, so that he wasn't loved even among his own Muslims. And especially after the elections, he was in the SDA party and he was among the leading extremists at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So he was involved in politics.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was a politician. And at the beginning -- or, rather, after the elections, cars were parked in front of his house marked as BH army vehicles. At the time this didn't interest me nor did I know what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So he was in the SDA leadership for Vitez municipality?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You said that your brother Dragan did occasionally wear a uniform, ever since the beginning of the war with the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, but not a complete uniform. Sometimes he would just wear a camouflage jacket that he had.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Were there any insignia on that uniform?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No, there were never any insignia on that uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that he owned and occasionally wore a black uniform?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did own a black uniform. It was given to him as a present by somebody whose vehicle he had prepared, because it was useful if he went to Zenica or somewhere else, he would not be stopped at the checkpoints, and that is why he would wear it sometimes, though it was too small for him. So I saw him wearing it very rarely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So it was a good idea to wear a black uniform if you went to Zenica?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, because the HOS was the only organised force in Zenica at the time, and all of them were wearing black uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: And why did he wear the camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: He wore it because everybody was wearing it. All young men were wearing uniforms. It was the fashion at the time just before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So young people who were not members of any particular units --

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, they would get them from their friends and they would wear them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did Dragan occasionally take part in village guard duty?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Maybe sometimes when someone was ill or when he didn't have to go to work in the morning, but this was very rarely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about the village guards in your area, how they were organised? Were they perhaps organised by any military structures? How did it all come about?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No, the local people, out of fear from the Serbs, they organised these village guards. They were people who organised themselves and who were protecting their families, because it happened in places that Serb extremists would break into a village and commit massacres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So as far as I understood, at first the guards were jointly -- guard duty was jointly kept?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, by Muslims and Croats together.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: How about the weapons of those guards?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: At first they mostly used hunting rifles and maybe a couple of M-48's, but no better equipment than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know that later on the guard split?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. When the Muslims organised their own party, the SDA party, they separated, they received weapons, they purchased weapons and they did everything to separate from us and, in fact, they did separate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you see something to the effect, as was stated here, that you were seen with your brother Dragan in the period in between the two conflicts and that Dragan had a strangling device in his hand?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: That is not true. That is absolutely not true. Maybe somebody said that we actually strangled somebody.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the day prior to the second conflict, that is, the 15th of April, 1993? Did anything special take place? Where was Dragan on that day, the 15th of April?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: On the 15th of April I was at school, Dragan was at work. In the afternoon we were at home. Nothing interesting took place. Nothing out of the ordinary. I don't know. I don't know how to put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So there were no indications that a conflict could break out the next day?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No, nothing at all. Everything was quite normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: What did you do that afternoon?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: I helped my brother a little in repairing a vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Now, tell us a little more about this second conflict on the 16th of April, 1993. Do you remember how things developed, what happened? Were you awakened by gunfire again in the morning?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: The 16th of April started with gunfire. It woke us up. And as we had lived through a similar conflict in October with the Muslims, we all got up. My father was frightened most of all. We all went into the kitchen from our bedrooms. We ran out of the house, we fled to the woods. We already found some neighbours there who had got there before us, my aunt Marija with her children. Just as we arrived in the woods, Ljubica Milicevic arrived with her children. She was crying. She didn't know what was happening because her husband had left for work. Then my father said to Dragan that he should take his wife, who was in advanced pregnancy, my sister, mother and the other women, that he should take them to Rovna. And as the fire was strong, we fled towards a stream at the end of the woods, and that is where we stayed all day until nightfall. In the night we returned home following that stream. We emerged near Ljubica Milicevic's house and we ran across the remaining distance to reach our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So you returned home during the night?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Why did you go to Ljubica Milicevic's?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Because we were following that stream that flowed right below her house. At the end of that stream there is a mild slope which takes you to her house, that you have to climb to reach her house.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So Dragan went to Donja Rovna?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. He took the women there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: The next day did you notice any damage on your house?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. The next day in the morning we realised what had happened there, and we saw damage done to many houses including our own.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: What do you think? How was that damage inflicted?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: I think it was inflicted by infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Where was the damage greatest?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: The greatest damage was on the roof. The minor damage was on the front facade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you repair the roof quickly?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, as soon as we came back to the house we had to repair the roof very soon after that to be able to live there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Could I ask the usher for his assistance, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D13/5.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Papic, is that your house?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Is the damage on the house visible?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: I can't see it well on this photograph. Something must be wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Well, look at the photograph itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Could the usher help me again, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D14/5.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Is this the front facade of your house, taken close up?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Could you mark with your pen, on this photograph that you see on the ELMO, the damage.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: (Marks) And all the damage is not visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: The usher's assistance, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D15/5.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Will you please mark the damage that is visible on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: (Marks).

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Where did this occur? What is this?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: This is the top part of the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Another photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D16/5.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mark the damage you see here.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: (Marks).

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Before that day, the 16th of April, your brother, Dragan Papic, do you know where he was?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I learned that my brother, Dragan, stayed to keep guard duty at Radak's bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know why Radak's bridge? It's an old bridge; why was it important? Why did it have to be guarded?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: The bridge as such provided the only communication line between Vitez and Busovaca on that day, because the Muslims had built a checkpoint at Buhine Kuce, a machine-gun nest, so passage was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Was this the only place of communication on that day, or throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Throughout the war, that was the only line of communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You said that the main road had been cut where?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: At Buhine Kuce.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: How had it been cut?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: The Muslims positioned a machine-gun nest there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So it was dangerous to pass by there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: How far is Buhine Kuce from Santici?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. Maybe 2 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that Dragan wore a beard at the time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, he had a long beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Was it longer than now?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was a much longer beard than he is wearing now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, we would like to show a videotape. Perhaps it would be better to do it after the break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Is it a videotape of the wedding?

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: No, no. It's a videotape of the family and an event. It is not the wedding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Are you suggesting that we should take a break now? Yes. All right. 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: --- Upon resuming at 12.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So I suggest we see a videotape taken in 1993, in the month of July. (Videotape played).

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Papic, who is this woman on the film?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: This woman is the mother of Ruzica, Dragan's wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: And who is she holding?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: She is holding Dragan's first child, Marjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So Marjan was about three months old then?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Will you play the video, please. (Videotape played).

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Fast forward, please. Stop. Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Papic, who do you recognise on this video?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: I recognise my brother, Dragan.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Is this the kind of beard that he wore at the time of the conflict in April 1993?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: It was even longer than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: And who is he holding?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: He's holding his son, Marijan.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So the tape was taken on the 18th of July, 1993, as indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: We can proceed, please. Play the tape. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Who is that on the left? You recognise Dragan?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think that is sufficient. That's all we need from this tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Papic, did Dragan later shave off his beard?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, he shaved it off when he baptised his son.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You said that that is his older son, Marijan; does he have another son?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, he has another son, who was born in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Can I ask the usher for his assistance, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The videotape was number D17/5, and this document is number D18/5.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Could the registrar please give us the number of the videotape -- 17; it's all right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Papic, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: This is a birth certificate of Marijan Papic, evidence of his birth.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: When was he born?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: In September 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Can we see the date?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: The 28th -- no, I'm sorry; April.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So this is 12 days after the conflict, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know where Marijan was born?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: He was born in Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: That is where?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: That is in the suburbs of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: And who delivered the baby?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Ulfeta Tuco, who followed the pregnancy of my sister-in-law, and Ruzica trusted her. She is Muslim. She was a midwife.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Usher, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D19/5.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Papic, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: It is the same kind of document, only it is a birth certificate for Dragan's son, Dejan.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: When was he born?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: On the 26th of September, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me whether ever, in front of your house or anywhere near it, there was a machine-gun nest, a machine gun, or an anti-aircraft gun?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No. As I said before, our house and the other houses were family homes, inhabited by older people: My own father, mother, my sister-in-law, who was pregnant; so this was not any kind of strategic location, nor were there any weapons there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did anyone from your house fire from a sniper?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No. Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did any one of you own a sniper rifle?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No. No one owned a sniper rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: What did Dragan own?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Dragan owned an ordinary rifle, an M-48, that he was given at work a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about Dragan shooting at any time at Muslim homes or threatening Muslims?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No, he never threatened Muslims, he never shot at Muslims. I don't know of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Dragan ever took part in a physical fight?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, I do not recall any incident involving him and someone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: What can you tell us about your brother as a person?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: He was a good-natured person. He would assist people that he could. He was not interested in politics. He was quite a good repairman for vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Was he ever convicted? Did he have a criminal record?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Usher, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D20/5.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Papic, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: This is a document certifying that Dragan Papic has not ever been convicted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Who issued the document?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: The police administration of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you know, was there a flag flying from your house all the time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No, during the Christmas holidays every household would hoist a Croatian flag, just as the Muslims would fly their own green flag for their holidays.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Was there any other kind of flag on your house?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No, never. There was never any other kind of flag on our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Were there cars around your house before the war and after the war?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: There were fewer before the war and since the war there are many more because before the war it was only my brother, and now I have continued his work after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether your brother, Dragan, had a Lada vehicle, a red Lada vehicle?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did own a red Lada vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when the car was purchased?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: I think it was purchased in 1995, towards the end of the war from the Vjetrenica company.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: The usher's assistance, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D21/5.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: What kind of document is this?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: It is a document on the buying and selling of the Lada vehicle that Dragan purchased from the Vjetrenica company.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Can you see the colour from the contract?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is red. And on the back side we can see the date when this document was certified. Yes, the 9th of January, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether your brother owned a car before?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. He had a Zastafa 101.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: What colour was it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: It was yellow.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I should like to ask the sound to be turned off or, rather, for us to go into private session for a few minutes only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. Granted. Private session. (Private session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: (Open session)

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone to the Prosecutor, please

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Papic. My name is Franck Terrier, I am one of the members of the Prosecution. I am going to put a number of questions to you concerning your testimony, the testimony you've just made before this Tribunal. Before getting to the events of that time period, please state what your present occupation is.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: My present occupation is that I sell spare parts for vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Who is your employer, Mr. Papic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: I am self-employed. I am the boss of my own shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Are you married?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You stated a moment ago that you lived in Vitez, unless I'm mistaken; is that correct? Were you working in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: I don't live in Vitez exactly but a suburb of Vitez called Santici in a place called Topala. I didn't understand your second question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: My question, sir, was with regards to the place in which you worked. Do you work in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No. Before the war I went to school.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Sir, the question I'm asking you, I'm not sure that we have understood one another, is to know where you are currently working. Where?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Currently I have a shop where I sell spare parts, and it's in my home in Topala in Santici.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: And your father, does he still work?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, my father still works. He maintains the water-mains for Vitez as far as the village of Nadioci. He maintains it all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Will you please show to the witness the document -- Prosecution Exhibit 61. We just showed it to him earlier. On the left of this photograph, sir, there is a red panel -- rather, a yellow panel with red letters. It seems to be some sort of a commercial billboard. We have other photographs, of course, of this billboard, but I'm using this one now for convenience's sake since we have it at hand. What does this sign state? Can you satisfied our curiosity in this regard?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: This sign states that these are scraps, car scraps and sale of spare parts and it shows my business.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: So this relates then to your own professional activity, your own business? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I would like for us to go back to the latter months of 1992 and the first months of 1993. In the beginning of 1993 you were 17 years of age?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: In early 1993. Just a moment. I was about sixteen and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Unless I'm mistaken about your date of birth, didn't you have your 18th birthday in December 1993?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Eighteen years of age, is that not the year of coming of age or the official year of age in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: At the end of 1992, early 1993, at that time you were living with your family, with your parents, your brother and your little sister?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. I lived with my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: How old was your little sister -- younger sister?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: My sister is older than me. She was born in 1970.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Pardon me. I apologise for that error. You stated, sir, that in the family climate of that time that there was no clear interest in politics. Can you please confirm this for me? Is this true? Is this exact?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. My father was a plumber, my mother was a housewife, and my sister worked in a shop owned by a relative and I went to school and no one was engaged in any kind of political activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Don't you have any memory of any discussions at the household or perhaps with your brother Dragan of the situation concerning the Croatian nation at that time or about the history of the Croatian nation?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: We never had such discussions at home. What we saw on television, in the media, we would sometimes comment on that a little but we never had any political discussions, especially before the war, in the pre-war period, or about pre-war politics.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You stated that your family, your brother, in particular your brother Dragan, had excellent relations with the Muslims living in Ahmici in particular, in particular with some of the neighbours. Did you not know that these excellent relations that existed before the war were transformed or deteriorated after the beginning of the war? In that I mean the last months of 1992 or the first months of 1993.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Relations never deteriorated with the Muslims. The relations changed among Muslims and Croats but never to any great extent. After the elections everyone -- the Muslims turned away from the Croats, the Croats from the Serbs, but we never had any problems. We lived normally with our neighbours who were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: When you talked about a change in these relations, to the best of your memory what are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Well, all I wanted to say was that Mehmed Ahmic Sudzuka got a position in the SDA party and he changed completely. He didn't want to communicate with the Croats, he didn't want to co-operate either in business or any other way. He avoided any kind of friendship. He avoided everything. We were very surprised by this, because in past years we had lived in a different way, but he was such a person that he did all sorts of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: But aside -- if we were to set aside the case of Mr. Ahmic, what about the case of Fahrudin Ahmic and the relations that you had with him and his family. Did they change?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: We were on good terms with him. We never had any bad relations with him, although the leading people in the village who were the political leaders were such that he was afraid to associate with us and we were surprised by this, but this was noticeable.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Therefore, to summarise your viewpoint, it seems that relations between Croats and Muslims within the village of Ahmici changed, became cooler and less frequent due to the facts as you've just stated, due to the fact that the Muslims themselves caused this to happen. Have I correctly summarised your viewpoint?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. The Muslims caused the change themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You stated, I believe, that your brother Dragan, and your father as well, had gone to the mosques on various solemn occasions. Do you recall the last time your brother and your father went to the mosque?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. A lot of time has passed since then.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand, of course. You stated that your father, who was a plumber, had done the plumbing in the two mosques in Ahmici. You presented this piece of information as evidence of the fact that your father had good relations with Muslims. I would like for you to tell me whether there were other plumbers in Ahmici, apart from your father.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No, there were no other plumbers in Ahmici except for my father. There were some in Vitez, but in the area of Santici, Nadioci, there was just my father.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Your father was paid for his work, was he not?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No, my father did this on a voluntary basis, of his own accord. He did not ask for payment. This was a gift to the religious building, the house of worship.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You told us about the first job that was occupied by Dragan before the war. Can you please explain for us what type of work it consisted of being a forester, and why would one need a firearm?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Dragan needed the job and he did it because he was educated for it, and he did it to support his wife and have his own income.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, of course, witness. I'm the not contesting that fact. I'm not asking you why he was working. I'm asking what his work consisted of and why he would need a weapon in the course of this work.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: His job consisted in preventing thefts from the forest, and he had to carry a weapon because of the wild animals which were especially aggressive during the winter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Who was Dragan Papic's employer?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: His employer was the Vitez forestry. The director was a Muslim from Kruscica, but I don't know his name. I've forgotten it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Do you recall up to what point your brother Dragan Papic carried out this work?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Dragan Papic carried out it this work until the 15th of April, 1993 in the forestry as a forester.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: And why on the days that followed, I'm not referring to the 16th, of course, but why in the days that followed did he not return to his work?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Because the war broke out and no one could continue doing their job. The conflict began between the Muslims and the Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: And what role did your brother Dragan play during that war?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: He did not have a role, he was only put there at the beginning of the war to guard Radak's bridge, to guard the bridge, to maintain the Vitez-Busovaca communication. After that his son was born, and after that he was sent to the frontline in Krtina Mahala somewhere. I think about 20 days after the conflict of the 16th of April. He was an ordinary soldier afterwards when he was sent to Krtina Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: So you're stating that after the 15th of April, 1993, I'm not going to specify the date to avoid any problems, but after that time period your brother became a soldier within the HVO and fought in the course of that work which took place during the months of 1993?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that. He didn't become a soldier on the 15th of March (sic). On the 15th of March (sic) he was only guarding Radak's bridge. After 20 days -- 20 days after he went to Radak's bridge he was assigned to Krtina Mahala. Before that he was just an ordinary guard guarding Radak's bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I understood, but to avoid having this type of discussion I'm not going to name any dates. Would you agree with me in saying that after that time period, and in particular when he was called upon to go to the frontline, at that point he became an HVO soldier and then fought as an HVO soldier during that war?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: On the 15th and 16th of March -- no, sorry, I mean April, he didn't get any kind of official notice to go to the frontline somewhere and to fight. It was only 20 days later that he was assigned to his post.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Once again, I don't want to trouble you in any way whatsoever, but what I wish to understand and the purpose of my question is to understand that within a certain time period in 1993, let's say 20 days after the 16th of April, 1993, of course, we're going to come back to this issue of dates, but for the time being I simply wish to understand whether some 20 days after the 16th of April, 1993, your brother indeed became a soldier within the HVO.

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes, he became a soldier like all the others who became soldiers who had not been soldiers up to that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Were you yourself a soldier within the HVO?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: I only became a soldier in late 1993, early 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Did you become an HVO soldier on the date you turned 18?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Maybe some two months after that. Maybe a month later. I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Did you volunteer, or were you called upon?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: I was mobilised. I was not a volunteer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: What role did you personally play within this war when you were called upon?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: I was at the front line in Barin Gaj. Like all the others, we were in trenches. I didn't have any extra tasks to do. I was just an ordinary soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 351.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Sir, would you please look at this document. It is a photocopy, photocopy of a register which was maintained by the HVO. We see now here the cover, photocopy of the cover, and a photocopy of the first page, and a blown-up photocopy of a page on which you find a list of names to which I'm going to draw your attention. Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: No. No, I haven't seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have only just received this document during the break, and we have not had time to study it or look at it, the document that the Prosecutor is referring to now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is a document which is quite simple on the face of it. It is indeed quite thick, if you see the entire document. However, there was only one page and indeed two lines which were of interest to us, and therefore we disclosed this document to the Defence before the beginning of the cross-examination. There are other documents which we felt should also be presented to this Trial Chamber during the course of the cross-examination. I hope the Trial Chamber will understand that a few days ago, I could not have imagined that I would be able to get a hold of such a document, or even need it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. I understand. In any case, Mr. Puliselic will have this afternoon to look through this document, because I don't imagine that we'll be able to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, you're right. I don't believe we will be able to finish with cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. So we will be able to continue tomorrow with cross-examination, and Mr. Puliselic will have the necessary time to ask questions and this afternoon can take advantage of this afternoon's break to look through and examine very closely the contents of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I also wish to add, Mr. President, that the Trial Chamber may understand that the guidelines, the directives of this Trial Chamber, sometimes indeed do pose certain problems with regards to the examination. We have tried to ensure that this document was submitted before the cross-examination, and that it only involves the accused in question here, whose counsel called this witness. So, if you will, it does not involve any of the other accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Witness, I'd like to draw your attention to the page which I believe is before you now, and in particular to the two names, 4628 and 4629. Witness, do you see these two names?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Let us begin with the name that is across from 4628. Here we see Iva Dragan Papic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: On the following column there is a number, identification number. There's a blank column, and then another column. We see the letter "P." Do you know what the "P "stands for?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: The two following columns, as we understand it, specify the time in which the person was engaged in these units. This can be verified by consulting the first page of this registry, or log. For Dragan Papic, we can see that his time of service started on the 8th of April, 1992, and lasted into 15 January, 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Terrier, what is your question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps my question was not a question; I will continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: My question was quite simply -- if it was a question -- to draw the witness's attention to these two columns. And in the first we see the starting point for the service in the unit, and the second column contains the last date of service within that unit. In other words, if we were to consult these two columns, we would understand that Iva Goran Papic was engaged on the 8th of April, 1992, until the 15th of January, 1996. Does this fact prompt any type of reaction or comment on your part?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: I don't know. This is not correct. What confuses me most is that there are women's names here. My sister's name is here, and some other female names. I don't understand the purpose of this document. I don't know what it was, because this is not correct at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I'll come back to that, Witness. I simply wish for you to understand-- to draw attention, rather, to the transcript. I talked about page 109, and talked about whether the -- I talked about Dragan Papic and not Goran Papic. Going back to that document again, can you see the signature, Dragan Papic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: I don't know what this is. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature as being that of your brother?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. I can't judge signatures.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Do you know your brother's signature?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember -- I've forgotten during this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Very well. On the line below that one, 4629, can you see the name "Papic, Iva Goran," engaged on the 16th of December, 1993, until the 15th of January, 1996? And on the right there is a signature, a handwritten signature. Do you recognise this signature as being your own?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: It does resemble my signature, but I don't remember ever having signed such a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Would you admit today, having examined this document, that it is indeed your signature?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't, because I never signed this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Let us be very clear, sir: Are you saying you don't remember having signed this document? Or are you asserting that you have never signed this document, and consequently what was written here has been falsified?

utterances.speaker: GORAN PAPIC
utterances.text: I didn't sign this document. But whether it has been falsified or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Do you have many more questions on this particular issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I wish to continue with this particular issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: No, but we have another hearing at 2.00, so unfortunately we must stop here. We will resume tomorrow at 9.00.
